restrictions: The online algorithm is deterministic replay of exactly the two 128-byte messages in proof.md; it is not a submitted generator for new collisions.
Use the standard fixed SHA-256 IV, original round indices 0 through 30 on every padded block, full eight-word feed-forward, FIPS padding, and all 256 output bits.

All historical characteristic search, failed work, table generation, matching, construction, and checking are charged once as preprocessing and included in total time; no cross-target amortization is claimed.
The score is conditional on H-HISTORICAL-TIME and H-HISTORICAL-MEMORY; neither bound has an authoritative organizer-model trace or resource receipt.

The organizer experiment checks only the exact collision relation. Repeated replay rows do not measure success probability, expected work, preprocessing, memory, novelty, or generator reproducibility.
This exploratory package claims no new cryptanalysis, no full-SHA-256 or 32-round collision, no lower security bound, and no rigorous qualification.

heuristics.statement: All computational work that led to the fixed witness, including differential-trail discovery, SAT/SMT and other tool runs, failed or abandoned trials, table construction, matching, message construction, and verification, is less than 2^127 collision-frontier-v3 charged units; total time after deterministic replay is less than 2^128 units.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the fixed two-message 31-round-prefix SHA-256 collision in proof.md, with all one-time historical construction paid once and no amortization across targets or outputs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Translate the primary publication's reported practical run and complexity, plus predecessor estimates, into a deliberately looser upper cap in the organizer's 256-bit word-RAM model, including omitted discovery and failure work.
heuristics.limitations: The located public material has no complete job ledger, instruction trace, resource receipt, practical generator, or record of every unsuccessful development run. Publication complexity units are not organizer word-RAM units. The large margin supports exploratory plausibility but does not prove the cap.

heuristics.statement: Peak simultaneously retained storage over every historical construction phase and deterministic replay is less than 2^36 bytes, including code, solver state, tables and indices, messages, advice, thread state, constants, and working storage.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the construction history and replay of the fixed witness in proof.md, including characteristic search and all practical-attack phases rather than only the final online program.
heuristics.extrapolation: Convert the reported 2^19.8 ten-word tuple table into packed bytes, allow even 64 full copies, and apply a further margin to cover indices, runtime, tools, and other retained state.
heuristics.limitations: The public report counts table entries rather than measured peak bytes and supplies no peak-resident-set trace. Allocator overhead, thread duplication, SAT/SMT state, characteristic search, and failed development runs are incompletely documented, so the 64 GiB cap remains plausible rather than certified.
